correctness.rationale: For independent common-target random mappings f(i)~p, write Z as sum of empty indegree indicators and T as pairwise 2-cycle indicators. On event f(i)=j,f(j)=i, the other n−2 arrows avoid each v outside {i,j} with probability (1−p_v)^(n−2). Summing p_i p_j yields exact Cov(Z,T)=((1+s2)V−2s2W)/2. If P assumes value p_i with probability p_i and h(t)=(1−t)^(n−2), monotonicity gives V=E[Ph(P)]≤E[P]E[h(P)]=s2 W. Thus Cov(Z,T)≤−s2(1−s2)W/2<0 when at least two positive p_i. Equality for n=2 (h constant) or equal positive probabilities for n>2 (h strictly decreasing). For fixed-point count F, conditional on any vertex absent, outgoing choices renormalize other p_j and E[F|I_v=1]=1, yielding Cov(Z,F)=0 even with zero weights. Independent exact Fraction enumeration checked n=3 uniform p=(1/3,1/3,1/3): −2/27, heterogeneous p=(1/2,1/3,1/6): −1/12, and p=(1/2,1/2,0): −1/16, plus zero Cov(Z,F). Source exact-rational checker was inspected, not treated as infinite proof.
